matchups.recap: Arben got absolutely skull-fucked this week, losing by 18 points to Rob while his roster collectively decided to take a nap. Whatever the hell you had plugged in at flex should've been left on the waiver wire where you found it, because this wasn't even close—it was a straight-up fantasy homicide. Better luck next week, champ, though at this rate you're gonna need a séance to resurrect this season.

Flamur got absolutely dicked down 130.9 to 112.4, and honestly that 18.5 point margin is generous because it makes this look competitive. Your team played like it was trying to tank for draft picks, except you're not even in the NBA—you're just bad at fantasy football. Next week maybe try starting players who actually show up instead of whatever zombie roster you sent out there.

Ben got absolutely obliterated by 69.3 points—which is fitting, because that's the only action his roster saw all week. He fielded a lineup that looked like he drafted with his eyes closed and then didn't check it until kickoff, while Rinor came in swinging a fully operational death star. Ben's team didn't just lose—it got surgically dismantled by nearly 70 points, the kind of ass-kicking that makes you wonder if he even set a lineup or just let the auto-draft algorithm make all his decisions for the whole damn season.

Veton got absolutely cock-teased by 3 fucking points, and you know what the worst part is? He'll spend all week replaying every decision like it matters, convincing himself one more waiver wire pickup would've saved him—spoiler alert, it wouldn't have. Adam sleepwalked to 112 and still beat you, which means somewhere deep down, you both know your team construction was dogshit. This is the kind of loss that keeps you up at night staring at your roster wondering where it all went wrong, probably around the 6th round when you panic-drafted like a man having a stroke.

Rilind got absolutely skull-fucked this week, losing by 25.3 points like he thought his bye-week players were gonna suit up and ball out. This wasn't a matchup, it was a mercy killing—Faton walked into your lineup and straight-up mugged you for a quarter-hundred points. You're out here looking like you autodrafted your entire bench, and frankly, that margin is the kindest thing that'll happen to you all season.

Ilir just got outscored by his own family member by 1.3 points—that's the fantasy football equivalent of losing a game of horse to your cousin and having to hear about it at every single family dinner for the next 12 months. Jetmir and Peter are gonna be walking around the Thanksgiving table like they own the place while Ilir sits there quietly dying inside, knowing he had a whole week to put up 95 points and still came up short against blood relatives. This is the kind of L that doesn't go away—this gets brought up at weddings, funerals, and every holiday gathering until one of you wins it back. Enjoy hearing "Remember when you lost by a point?" for the rest of your natural life, buddy.

matchups.preview: Rob's out here looking like he's actively trying to lose fantasy football while Nori's actually figured out how to read a roster. Rob's 1-4 ass is about to get absolutely humiliated by someone who knows what a waiver wire is—Nori's 4-1 squad is going to walk all over you like you're a FAAB budget sheet you already fucked up.

Ben's sitting at 2-3 playing like he grabbed his entire roster from the waiver wire in Week 8, and now he's got the pleasure of facing Arben's 4-1 squad that's actually managed to not completely implode—yet. This is the matchup where Ben's usual incompetence gets exposed on a national stage, because Arben's been riding a wave of competence that Ben can't even comprehend from his basement dwelling at .500.

Veton's 0-5 dumpster fire is about to meet the only team in this league playing competent football, and honestly, this feels less like a matchup and more like a mercy killing—Flamur's gonna put up 180 and Veton will still manage to lose by 40 while his studs underperform like they're running through mud. At this point Veton should just surrender his roster to the waiver wire Gods and pray for next season, because this week's gonna be the most lopsided beatdown we've seen all year.

Faton's sitting pretty at 3-2, but we all know that record is held together with duct tape and prayers — one bad week and this whole thing collapses like his draft strategy did in round four. Rinor's matching that record with what has to be the most uninspired roster construction this side of a bye week, so whoever chokes first gets the honor of being the least impressive 3-2 team in league history. This is going to be a masterclass in mediocrity, and honestly, we're all just here to watch which one finds new and creative ways to fuck it up.

Ilir's sitting pretty at 3-2, which is hilarious because it's basically the participation trophy of records—good enough to not be embarrassing, bad enough that everyone knows you're getting bounced in the playoffs. Adam's limping in at 2-3 like a guy who traded his first-round pick for a handshake, so this matchup is essentially "mediocrity vs. slightly-more-mediocrity," and somehow both of you are gonna find a way to lose this anyway.

Jetmir's 3-2 record is held together with duct tape and prayer, while Rilind's 1-4 dumpster fire limps into this matchup like a team that thought drafting three RBs in the first four rounds was "value." One of these teams is about to get exposed, and Rilind's been getting exposed all season—this is just his weekly reminder that his team management makes a monkey with a dartboard look like a genius.
